title: Ramp Alternatives 2026: Pricing and Plans Compared
h1: Ramp Alternatives 2026: Card Fees and Software Plans Compared
metaDescription: Ramp alternatives for corporate cards and spend management: Brex, Mercury, Relay, Expensify and BILL, with published plan fees, wire costs and credit lines.
intro:
Brex, Mercury, Relay, Expensify and BILL are the five business money tools covered as Ramp alternatives. Published entry prices are $0 at Ramp Free, Brex Essentials, Mercury, Relay Starter, Expensify Submit and BILL Spend & Expense. Paid plans run from $5 per member per month on Expensify Collect to $12 on Brex Premium and $15 on Ramp Plus.

[Ramp](https://www.ramp.com/pricing) sells a Free plan at $0 per user per month with corporate cards, unlimited cards, travel and expense management, and accounts payable bill payment by Automated Clearing House (ACH), card, check and wire. Ramp Plus lists at $15 per user per month plus an unpublished team-size platform fee (with a 20% discount on annual billing), adding multi-entity support, artificial intelligence (AI) expense reviews, custom user roles and integrations for NetSuite and Sage Intacct. Ramp also lists a footnoted 4.61% yield in a Ramp Investment Account with no fees, minimum deposits or transfer caps, alongside 2% on cash in a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) insured checking account.

 For related banking and card shortlists, read our [best business bank accounts roundup](/roundup/best-business-bank-accounts/), our [best business credit cards roundup](/roundup/best-business-credit-cards/) and our [best accounting software for freelancers](/roundup/best-accounting-software-for-freelancers/) guide. You can also review our [Brex alternatives](/alternatives/brex/) guide, our [Mercury alternatives](/alternatives/mercury/) comparison and our [comparison hub](/compare/).

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a Ramp Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Choosing a Ramp alternative starts with deciding whether your business needs corporate cards, payment processing, savings yields, or spend management software. Ramp bundles corporate cards with unlimited cards, invoice creation, travel and expense management, and accounts payable bill payment. Alternatives separate these tasks across different pricing models.

First, check how each provider charges for user access. Ramp Free allows unlimited cards and expense management for $0 per user per month, while Ramp Plus charges $15 per user per month plus a platform fee based on team size. Brex offers its Essentials tier at $0 per user per month and charges $12 per user per month for Brex Premium. Expensify charges $5 per member per month on Collect. In contrast, Mercury charges flat monthly account prices rather than per-user rates: Mercury base costs $0, Mercury Plus costs $29.90 per month billed annually ($35 per month month-to-month), and Mercury Pro costs $299 per month billed annually ($350 per month month-to-month). Relay Starter charges $0 per month and includes unlimited user seats.

Second, compare payment execution fees. Ramp provides free wires and same-day ACH payments through its Bill Pay tools. Mercury includes free Automated Clearing House transfers, wire transfers in United States dollars (USD), and check mailing on its $0 base plan. Relay states on its pricing page that it saves businesses up to 50% over competitors on wire and same-day ACH payments. BILL lists transaction fees of $0.59 and $1.99 per payment, with the $1.99 fee applying when BILL mails the check.

Third, examine cash yields and account balances. Ramp lists a footnoted 4.61% variable yield in a Ramp Investment Account with no minimum deposits or transfer caps, alongside 2% on cash in an FDIC-insured checking account. Relay Starter provides a 1.19% APY on savings, Relay Grow lists 1.87% APY, and Relay Scale lists 3.21% APY. Brex footnotes an estimated 3.64% to 3.99% treasury return rather than checking APY, while Expensify lists no cash yields.

Before choosing a Ramp alternative, run through these five checks:

- How many employees need a card or an expense login, and does the plan charge per seat or a flat monthly account fee?
- Does your company send domestic wire transfers or paper checks every month, and what does each provider charge per transaction?
- Does your accounting workflow require QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite or Sage Intacct?
- Do you need an integrated commercial checking account, or do you prefer corporate cards linked to an existing external bank account?
- Does your finance team require multi-entity consolidation, custom user roles or procurement add-ons?

alternatives.heading: Brex Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Brex provides corporate cards, global expense controls, travel booking and spend management. Brex LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Capital One, N.A. Brex divides its software into Essentials, Premium and Enterprise tiers. Brex Essentials costs $0 per user per month and covers global card acceptance, local currency wire transfers, accounting integrations and free travel booking. Brex Premium costs $12 per user per month and adds multiple customizable expense policies, enterprise resource planning (ERP) integrations and human resources information system (HRIS) integrations. Brex Enterprise uses custom pricing.

Brex fits businesses that need corporate cards with global acceptance, travel booking and customizable expense policies.

 Ramp Plus integrates with NetSuite and Sage Intacct for $15 per user per month plus a team-size platform fee, whereas Brex includes advanced ERP connections in Brex Premium at $12 per user per month or custom Enterprise plans. Ramp also lists a 4.61% variable yield in a Ramp Investment Account and 2% on cash in an FDIC-insured checking account, while Brex footnotes an estimated total treasury return between 3.64% and 3.99% (an annualized variable estimate, not a checking APY).

Worked cost example: For a 10-user team, Brex Essentials costs $0 per year ($0 x 10 x 12). On Brex Premium, that 10-user team pays $12 per user per month, which totals $120 per month or $1,440 per year ($12 x 10 x 12). On Ramp Plus, 10 users cost $150 per month ($15 x 10), which totals $1,800 per year before adding Ramp's unpublished platform fee based on team size. Ramp Free costs $0 for the same 10 users. These figures are arithmetic on list prices for a 10-user example, not quotes.

alternatives.heading: Mercury Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Mercury provides company cards, expense management tools, and payment services. Mercury's pricing page defaults to annual billing with a 15% discount. The Mercury base plan costs $0 per month with no monthly service fees and no minimum balance rules. It includes company cards, expense management, free ACH payments, free checks and free wires in USD. Mercury Plus costs $29.90 per month billed annually, or $35 per month on month-to-month billing. Mercury Plus adds a 30-day free trial and invoicing with ACH debit collection at $1 per transaction. Mercury Pro costs $299 per month billed annually, or $350 per month on month-to-month billing, and reduces ACH debit invoicing to $0 per transaction. Optional add-ons include Mercury Books at $35 per month and Mercury Payroll at $100 per month plus $50 per person paid per month, with both add-on fees waived until December 31, 2026.

Mercury fits businesses that want company cards, expense management and free USD wire transfers under a flat monthly plan rather than per-seat software pricing.

Versus Ramp, Ramp offers procurement as an add-on to Plus, while Mercury includes company cards and expense management on its base tier. Ramp provides travel and expense management, accounts payable bill pay by ACH, card, check and wire, unlimited cards, and invoice creation on its $0 Free tier. Ramp Plus adds procurement as an add-on, multi-entity support and AI expense reviews. Mercury includes company cards and expense management on its base tier, but requires Mercury Plus ($29.90 per month billed annually or $35 monthly) or Mercury Pro ($299 per month billed annually or $350 monthly) for invoicing with ACH debit.

Worked cost example: A company with 10 team members using Mercury base pays $0 per year in software maintenance fees. On Mercury Plus, the annual cost is $358.80 billed annually ($29.90 x 12), or $420 per year when paid month-to-month ($35 x 12). On Mercury Pro, the cost is $3,588 per year billed annually ($299 x 12), or $4,200 per year paid month-to-month ($350 x 12). On Ramp Plus, 10 users cost $1,800 per year ($15 x 10 x 12) before Ramp's unpublished team-size platform fee, while Ramp Free costs $0. These figures are arithmetic on list prices for a 10-user example, not quotes.

alternatives.heading: Relay Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Relay provides savings accounts and credit cards with integrated payment tools. Relay Starter costs $0 per month and includes unlimited user seats, 1.19% APY on savings (footnoted on its pricing page), and 1% cash back on credit cards (footnoted). Relay also offers Grow and Scale tiers with free trials. Relay Grow provides 1.87% APY on savings and 1.25% cash back on credit cards. Relay Scale provides 3.21% APY on savings and 1.5% cash back on credit cards. Relay Grow and Scale monthly prices are shown on Relay's pricing page. Relay states that it saves customers up to 50% over competitors on wire transfers and same-day ACH payments.

Relay fits small business owners who want unlimited user seats, savings interest and credit card cash back. Ramp provides unlimited corporate cards, travel and expense tracking, bill payment by card, check, wire and ACH, invoice creation, and accounts receivable tools on its $0 Free plan. Relay focuses on savings accounts and credit cards, while stating it saves up to 50% over competitors on wire and same-day ACH. Ramp lists a footnoted 4.61% variable yield in an investment account, while Relay Scale lists a 3.21% APY on savings.

Worked cost example: A 10-person business on Relay Starter pays $0 per month in software subscription fees, totaling $0 per year. That same 10-person business pays $0 per year on Ramp Free. If the team upgrades to Ramp Plus, the subscription cost is $1,800 per year ($15 x 10 x 12) before Ramp's team-size platform fee. Relay Grow and Scale monthly prices are shown on Relay's pricing page, so full annual totals for those tiers are omitted here. These figures are arithmetic on list prices for a 10-user example, not quotes.

alternatives.heading: Expensify Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Expensify provides expense tracking, receipt management and employee reimbursement software. Expensify offers three primary service levels: Submit, Collect and Control. Expensify Submit is a free tier that covers receipt SmartScan, mileage tracking and basic expense reports. Expensify Collect costs $5 per member per month. Expensify Control uses custom pricing, listed on its pricing page as low as $9 per member per month. Expensify includes a 30-day free trial.

Expensify fits businesses and traveling employees whose primary requirement is scanning paper receipts, tracking vehicle mileage and submitting expense reports.

Versus Ramp, Expensify falls short on native banking and accounts payable payment breadth. Expensify charges $5 per member per month on Collect. Ramp includes unlimited corporate cards, accounts payable bill pay by ACH, card, check and wire, invoice creation, and QuickBooks Online and Xero integrations on its $0 Free plan. Expensify does not provide checking accounts or cash interest yields on its pricing page, whereas Ramp lists 2% on cash in an FDIC-insured checking account and 4.61% in a Ramp Investment Account.

Worked cost example: A team of 10 employees on Expensify Collect pays $5 per member per month, which equals $50 per month or $600 per year ($5 x 10 x 12). On Ramp Free, that same 10-person team pays $0 per year. On Ramp Plus, 10 users pay $1,800 per year ($15 x 10 x 12) before Ramp's unpublished team-size platform fee. These figures are arithmetic on list prices for a 10-user example, not quotes.

alternatives.heading: BILL Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
BILL provides payment processing, 1099 filings and business credit lines. BILL offers four service tiers: Essentials, Team, Corporate and Enterprise, with custom pricing on Enterprise. BILL publishes plan prices on its pricing page. BILL advertises payment processing fees of $0.59 and $1.99 per payment, with the $1.99 fee applying when BILL mails the check. It also lists 1099 filings at $2.99 per 1099 for IRS e-filing ($1.99 via Accountant Console, $1.49 state filing, $1.99 mail delivery) and credit lines from $1,000 to $5M.

BILL fits companies that prioritize payment processing, check mailing, 1099 filings, and access to commercial lines of credit up to $5M.

Versus Ramp, BILL packages accounts payable and spend management across separate plans. Ramp includes corporate cards with unlimited cards, travel and expense management, invoice creation, accounts receivable tools, and free wires and same-day ACH via Bill Pay on its $0 Free tier. BILL applies transaction fees of $0.59 and $1.99 per bill payment, and $2.99 per 1099 IRS e-filing. BILL also offers a Spend & Expense plan at $0 per user per month that includes corporate cards, budgets and expense tracking.

Worked cost example: BILL prices its accounts payable and accounts receivable plans per user per month, with figures published on its pricing page. Ramp includes free wires and same-day ACH inside its Bill Pay feature on its $0 Free tier.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
Ramp and its alternatives do not suit every business profile. Review these exclusions before making an operational change:



- Businesses that require published, low-cost enterprise accounting connections without paying per-seat software fees fit poorly with Ramp Plus, which charges $15 per user per month plus an unpublished team-size platform fee for NetSuite and Sage Intacct integrations.
- Teams requiring global card acceptance and local currency wires at $0 per user per month fit Brex Essentials rather than Ramp Free.
- Organizations needing commercial borrowing lines exceeding $5M cannot obtain that financing through BILL, which advertises credit lines up to $5M.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer
alternatives.body:
The comparison on this page reflects published pricing and features checked on November 26, 2026. Several potential moves by these providers would alter how they compare:

- If Ramp introduces mandatory software subscription fees on its Free plan or removes free wire transfers from Bill Pay, its cost advantage over Expensify and Brex would decrease.
- If Ramp publishes specific dollar rates for its team-size platform fee on Ramp Plus, annual budget comparisons against Brex Premium could be calculated precisely.
- If Brex raises its $12 per user per month price on Brex Premium or adds booking fees to travel on Brex Essentials, its competitive standing would shift.
- If Mercury ends its fee waivers for Mercury Books ($35 per month) and Mercury Payroll ($100 per month plus $50 per person) after December 31, 2026, add-on subscription fees will apply.
- If Relay publishes lower transaction costs or alters its savings yields from 1.19% on Starter, 1.87% on Grow, and 3.21% on Scale, deposit yield calculations would need revision.
- If BILL removes its $0.59 and $1.99 payment fees or publishes lower subscription tiers, its accounts payable cost comparison against Ramp Bill Pay would shift.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Ramp Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Ramp remains the closer fit for businesses that want an all-in-one corporate card, spend management and accounts payable platform with no mandatory monthly subscription fees. Ramp Free costs $0 per user per month and provides unlimited corporate cards, travel and expense tracking, budgets and reporting, invoice creation, and accounts receivable tools. It also integrates with QuickBooks Online and Xero at no extra charge.

Ramp Bill Pay includes free wires and same-day ACH transfers, allowing finance teams to pay vendor invoices by ACH, card, check or wire without paying the $0.59 or $1.99 per-transaction fees listed by BILL. On the cash management side, Ramp lists a footnoted 4.61% variable yield in a Ramp Investment Account with zero fees, no minimum deposits and no transfer caps, alongside 2% on cash balances held in an FDIC-insured checking account.

Ramp Plus costs $15 per user per month plus a platform fee based on team size (with 20% savings on annual billing). Ramp Plus adds multi-entity management, custom user roles, an audit log, AI expense reviews, procurement add-ons, and direct connections to NetSuite and Sage Intacct.

verdict: Ramp provides $0 corporate cards, expense management and free bill pay by wire and ACH, while Brex Essentials delivers $0 cards with free travel booking, and Mercury offers a $0 base plan with free USD wire transfers. Relay pairs savings yields up to 3.21% APY with credit card cash back, Expensify starts at $5 per member per month on Collect for receipt tracking, and BILL provides payment processing with credit lines up to $5M. To evaluate Ramp alternatives for your company, count your active cardholders, calculate your monthly wire and check volume, and compare the published rates in the table above.

faqs.question: What should I use instead of Ramp?
faqs.answer: The main Ramp alternatives are Brex, Mercury, Relay, Expensify and BILL. Brex Essentials offers corporate cards and travel booking at $0 per user per month. Mercury provides a base plan with free USD wires for $0 per month. Relay offers up to 3.21% APY on savings, Expensify covers receipt management from $5 per member per month on Collect, and BILL provides payment processing.

faqs.question: Is Ramp free to use?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ramp offers a Free plan at $0 per user per month that includes unlimited corporate cards, travel and expense tracking, accounts payable bill payment by ACH, card, check and wire, and QuickBooks Online and Xero integrations. Ramp Plus costs $15 per user per month plus a team-size platform fee.

faqs.question: How does Ramp pricing compare with Brex?
faqs.answer: Both Ramp Free and Brex Essentials cost $0 per user per month. For paid plans, Brex Premium costs $12 per user per month, while Ramp Plus costs $15 per user per month plus an unpublished platform fee based on team size (with 20% off for annual billing). On a 10-user team, Brex Premium costs $1,440 per year, while Ramp Plus costs $1,800 per year before Ramp's platform fee.

faqs.question: Does Mercury charge per user like Ramp?
faqs.answer: No. Mercury charges flat monthly fees per company account rather than per-user fees. Mercury base costs $0 per month, Mercury Plus costs $29.90 per month billed annually ($35 per month month-to-month), and Mercury Pro costs $299 per month billed annually ($350 per month month-to-month). All Mercury plans include company cards and expense tools.

faqs.question: What fees does BILL charge compared to Ramp Bill Pay?
faqs.answer: Ramp Bill Pay includes free wires and free same-day ACH transfers on its $0 Free tier. BILL publishes plan prices on its pricing page and lists payment processing fees of $0.59 and $1.99 per transaction ($1.99 when BILL prints and mails a check), alongside $2.99 per 1099 IRS e-filing.
